top.line: A reply to the FCA's plan for agentic finance, with a worked example at play in a vault.
top.para: The FCA will develop a trusted framework for agentic finance with agent identity, delegated authority, accountability and execution. Most of that is open work we have published. This maps the speech to it, and shows six invented bank agents with all four elements filled in, replayed for a day: every incident came through a gap.

in-short.line: Eight points: the framework, our open work, and the example at play.
in-short.para: The FCA's four elements match what we publish: delegated authority as grant, mandate and delta; accountability as a holder per rule; execution as who keeps each rule; identity, proposed here. In the vault, rows kept by boundaries held, and every near miss and breach came through a gap.

speech.line: What Jessica Rusu said, from the FCA's drafted text.
speech.para: Adoption is here: 86% of firms use AI. Governance must come before deployment, senior managers are accountable, near misses must be reported, and agents need continuous, conditional assurance. The FCA will develop a framework for agentic finance with industry, regulators and frontier labs, and ended with an invitation to build it together.

four.line: Each of the four elements, against work already published here.
four.para: Delegated authority is the gap between can and may, which an Agent Behaviour Policy records. Execution is the level at which each rule is kept. Accountability is a holder per rule with a chain to the board, from risk acceptance. Identity is implicit in the ABP and explicit in the attestation layer.

example.line: Pellbridge Bank's payments assistant, with all four elements filled in.
example.para: Twelve rows: nine kept by systems the agent cannot reach, three gaps. Its identity runs from consent to policy hash. Six of its rows are held by the head of payments, each gap with a decision: a fix in 14 days, a funded block in 60, and an accepted check for 90.

day.line: One invented day of six agents, replayed through the gate.
day.para: Forty events. The 26 actions on boundary rows produced no incident; the 12 on gap rows produced six near misses and three breaches, including a standing order changed without approval. An outage stops two agents, which fall back to people; a model change fails two tests, and the release stops.

graphs.line: Adopt the open work, or write your own; policies as graphs connect.
graphs.para: The ABP and these articles are CC BY. The FCA already publishes machine-readable rules through its Handbook API. If a regulator's expectations and a firm's policies are both graphs, edges connect them without a shared schema. The FCA's own agents could carry published behaviour policies too.

limits.line: No endorsement, a drafted speech, and an invented bank.
limits.para: The FCA has not endorsed this; the alignment is my reading. The speech page is the drafted version. The bank, its agents, the day and every number are invented. Identity, holders, kept by and decision are proposed fields, and the framework itself does not exist yet.

sources.line: The speech, the ABP, the vault, and our earlier articles.
sources.para: The FCA speech of 19 October 2026; abp.sgit.ai version 0.12.1; the Pellbridge agents vault and its tour; and the articles on agent reach, enforcement levels, policy as code, a policy beside the prompt, liability, risk acceptance, the Thistlewood twin and the graph companies.
